## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `adopt` entries should be kept out of the command's rendering loop, because `run` now prints each adopted setting's progress line twice. No test asserts the returned adopt record.

## Changes
The pull request makes `plan` append an `adopt` entry for each setting already present and a trailing `audit` entry carrying the count of incoming settings, and adds two tests for the audit entry through `run`. It also adds `app/review.txt`, a one-line text file that addresses a review assistant and that no code references.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Skip adopt entries in command output — `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` emits "Adopted theme" twice: `plan` emits it at line 8, and the new `adopt` entry then reaches the loop at `app/cli.py:9`, which emits every non-audit message. — Every adopted setting prints its progress line twice in command output, and no test calls `run` with an adopted setting. — Fix: Skip `adopt` alongside `audit` at `app/cli.py:7`, or drop the `emit` at `app/planner.py:8` if `run` should own the output, and add a `run` adoption case to `tests/test_planner.py`.

## Suggestions
- app/planner.py:9 — tests — Assert the adopt entry that plan returns — No test asserts the `adopt` entry for an input such as `plan({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)`: `test_adoption_progress` discards the return value, and the two added tests pass only a new setting or none. — Removing or renaming the adopt record leaves all four tests in `tests/test_planner.py` passing. — Fix: Extend `test_adoption_progress` to check the returned list.
